module: GE extension `core_vehicle_triggerLabelPlacement`: computes where to place the UI label of a vehicle trigger (jbeam interaction zones) around its box projected on screen. Rebuilds the trigger's basis (axes) from the idRef/idX/idY nodes and its rotations (reproducing the C++ code's sequence), derives the half-dimensions, projects the 8 corners onto the screen and picks the side (right, left, top, bottom) with the most room. Utility functions with no persistent state, used by the trigger UI/debug tools and by core_vehicle_vehicleTriggerHighlight.
notes: Screen coordinates are fractions 0..1 (worldToScreenPercent01 must return a {x, y} table in this range). The tables returned by computeForTrigger are reused from one call to the next (no copy): the caller must consume or copy the result right away.
The side is 'bottom' if the projected box fits entirely in the central 15%-85% zone of the screen; otherwise it is the side that offers the most free space.

Trigger size: a number gives a sphere of half-dimension |size|; a table/vector is read as full dimensions (converted to half-dimensions, default 0.2). Angles whose value exceeds 2π are considered to be degrees.
If idRef/idX/idY are missing or degenerate, the basis falls back to the world axes (1,0,0), (0,1,0), (0,0,1).

computeForTrigger.desc: Computes the placement of a trigger's label: projects the trigger's box on screen and chooses the label side with its position (labelX, labelY as screen fraction) and CSS offsets (labelTx, labelTy, with 0.6em margin).

triggerObj.desc: trigger object (getCenter method); unnecessary if centerWorld is provided

triggerData.desc: trigger jbeam data (idRef, idX, idY, size, baseRotation, rotation...)

worldToScreenPercent01.desc: function(worldPos, output) -> {x, y} in screen fractions

p.desc: optional profiler (add method) to measure the steps

centerWorld.desc: trigger center in world space (otherwise triggerObj:getCenter())

centerScreen.desc: center on screen, already computed (otherwise computed via worldToScreenPercent01)

returns.desc: {labelX, labelY, labelTx, labelTy, labelSide ('right'|'left'|'top'|'bottom'), bounds = {minX, maxX, minY, maxY, centerX, centerY}}; nil if projection is impossible

computeTriggerBasisAndHalfExtents.desc: Returns the trigger's orthonormal basis and its half-dimensions, shared with the debug/highlight drawings to stay consistent with the placement.
